limitations: No supplements; Table 1 present in source.json and every row used. Six figures inspected in the visual submission; the annotation figure rows keep the caption-layer not_inspected convention.
All patients are cats (nonhuman). Breed is carried in case_context descriptions because the demographics schema has no breed attribute.

Source conflicts quarantined as review-only facts: Patient 2 conjunctival lesion eye (text left, Table 1 right); Patient 4 conjunctival site (lower palpebral versus third eyelid) and corneal laterality (same eye versus contralateral), both from the discussion; Patient 5 plaque color (brown in text, black in Table 1).

Series statements not copied to individuals because the covered set is unclear or counts only: "In all cases, an amorphous black plaque" (four additional cases or all five), three of four cases with ipsilateral corneal sequestra (Table 1 lists Patient 3 as contralateral), three cases with ulceration, entropion in three of four cases, and inflammatory cells and microorganisms in the surrounding propria.

Statements covering all five patients explicitly were copied to each: histology of all five conjunctival lesions, unknown infectious disease status, no recurrence in any case, and no known history of listed causes of conjunctival necrosis (kept review-only because detailed history was missing for some cases).
Surgical instruments, brand names, specimen fixation, and the corneal sequestrum histology availability counts are not recorded as separate facts.
Table 1 footnote a (archive source anonymized) is administrative and not recorded.

Series counts that disagree with the individual descriptions were not copied: "Three of the cases had conjunctival ulceration" while the case texts and captions report ulceration for Patients 1, 2, 4 and 5 and intact epithelium for Patient 3; "Three of the four cases also had corneal sequestra ipsilaterally" while Table 1 lists ipsilateral for Patients 2 and 4, contralateral for Patient 3 and absent for Patient 5.
No literal order links presentation and excision/histology for Patients 2, 4 and 5 (paragraph order only), so those events carry no relations.

caption_claims.text:
FIGURE 2
(A) Histologic section of the corneal plaque removed by superficial lamellar keratectomy in Patient 1. There is brownish discoloration and compaction of the collagen lamellae and lack of viable keratocytes in the affected area (arrow). Inflammatory cells infiltrate the surrounding stroma (asterisk). The surface (top of the image) lacks epithelium (ulceration). Hematoxylin and eosin stained. Scale bar 100 μm. (B, C) Histologic section of the dark conjunctival lesion removed by excisional biopsy in Patient 1. (B) The overlying conjunctival epithelium is discontinuous (ulceration) (black arrow) and separated from the sequestrum (indicated by white asterisk). Hematoxylin and eosin stained. Scale bar 100 μm. (C) There is brownish discoloration and compaction of the collagen and lack of viable fibroblasts in the sequestrum and an abrupt transition between affected and unaffected tissue. A small number of inflammatory cells and nuclear debris occupy the surrounding substantia propria. Hematoxylin and eosin stained. Scale bar 20 μm.
